_units: env_irradiance / irradiance = Blender W/m^2 on a surface facing the source (sun lamp Strength units). Area-light power is derived as P = E*pi*d^2 (Lambertian far-field), so moving a light never changes its irradiance at the target. azimuth_deg is measured from the camera->target direction around world Z (0 = light at camera, +90 = camera-left/right per sign), elevation_deg above the target's horizon.
_white_balance: Camera white balance defaults to the irradiance-weighted mired mean of the preset lamps (sun, rig, practicals); white_balance_k pins it (interior/night keep some warmth on purpose).
_sun_ratio: exterior_day means direct-sun-dominant: the HDRI's measured sun:sky ratio is clamped to [4,10]; overcast looks need their own preset, not a lower clamp.
_exposure: meter_key is the scene-linear log-average luminance the metering pre-render is driven to (0.18 = mid-grey). exposure = log2(meter_key / measured), clamped to exposure_clamp_ev. This keeps exposure from drifting when the HDRI or scene scale changes.

camera_sky._note: camera-only dusk gradient (reference: deep blue zenith, orange-pink glow at the horizon); the HDRI still lights the scene. Strength = level * 2^-EV.

meter_highlight._note: highlight priority: lit windows and lamps (top 0.5 % of the subject) stay under max_linear after exposure; measured s01: the log-average meter re-raised EV whenever windows were dimmed. 0.6 (2026-10-06, unmeasured until the next render): at the 160 px meter a window shares its pixel with wall, so the measured top is about a third of its true radiance and 2.0 never bound
